summary: - _(c) Pass any other or further orders which this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of this case._ 13. The matter was heard for the first time on 23.10.2024, on admission. On a query by the Commission as to whether the consent of the beneficiaries for the life extension has been sought, the learned counsel clarified that the Respondents could indicate their stand on this issue in their replies to be filed on the proposal of the Petitioner. Accordingly, the Petition was admitted. 14. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner made oral submissions on the matter. On the specific query of the Commission as to whether the Petitioner has obtained the consent of the beneficiaries, the learned counsel clarified that, though the beneficiaries 15. The representative for the Respondent, APDCL, sought time to file its reply in the matter. The Commission, after hearing the parties, permitted the Respondents to file their replies, after serving a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder. Subject to the above and based on the consent of the parties, the Commission reserved its order in the Petition. - (vii) In accordance with Regulation 27, any Renovation and Modernization (R&M) proposal aimed at extending the life of the project beyond its originally recognized useful life mandates prior consent from beneficiaries. It is crucial to highlight that the Petitioner has not obtained the written consent of APDCL, nor has any such proposal been agreed upon. Therefore, the petition filed without the explicit consent of APDCL is in contravention of the regulatory framework, and such omission must be duly considered by the Hon’ble Commission in assessing the admissibility of the petition. - (viii) Regulation 27(2) clearly outlines that the Commission, before granting approval, must consider various factors, including the consent of beneficiaries. It is submitted that APDCL’s consent is a significant factor and should weigh heavily against any proposed approval by the Hon’ble Commission. The importance of beneficiary agreement is implicit in ensuring transparency, fairness, and economic prudence. 17. In response to the above reply filed by the Respondent APDCL, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 19.5.2025 in its rejoinder has submitted that all averments made by the APDCL are specifically denied to the extent of their inconsistency with the instant Petition. Nothing stated by the APDCL in the Reply shall be deemed to have been admitted by NEEPCO unless the same has been specifically admitted and submitted that the reply filed by APDCL is devoid of merit. The Petitioner, in its rejoinder, has mainly submitted as under: 24. The Petitioner, further issued Public Notices on 28.1.2025 seeking consent of the beneficiaries with respect to the life extension of the Assam Gas Based Power Station (‘AGBPS’) beyond its useful life. The Petitioner had issued the public notices in different newspapers of different states of the beneficiaries (i.e. The Shillong Times, Dainik Sambad, Agartala, The Assam Tribune, The Arunachal Times, The Sangai Express and The Nagaland Post) 25. In terms of the said Notices, opportunity had been granted to the beneficiaries to offer their comments/objections, if any. The stakeholders had also been put on notice that, in the event no comments were received within the stipulated period, then it would be construed as consent. The Petitioner has submitted that no objections/comments have been filed in response to the said Notices. issued by the Petitioner seeking consent of the beneficiaries with respect to the life extension of life. _The forum acknowledged NEEPCO's proposal and expressed its interest in seeking the consent of NER Beneficiaries individually. All the States present in the meeting agreed in-principle for the R & M of the Power Station. However, it was decided that NEEPCO would take written consent from all beneficiaries individually._ 37. Through these notices, stakeholders were invited to submit their comments or objections, if any, within the stipulated time period. The notices also clearly stated that in the absence of any response, it would be presumed that there were no objections and that consent was deemed to have been granted. The Petitioner has confirmed that no comments or objections were received in response to the public notices. 38. The Respondent APDCL, in its affidavit dated 9.5.2025, has acknowledged that the power from the project has been regularly scheduled. However, this is solely because the allocation has not been formally withdrawn by the Ministry of Power. Such continued scheduling should not be misconstrued as an endorsement or willingness to remain a beneficiary of the project. The main concern of the respondent is the steep and sustained increase in Energy charges, which directly impacts consumer tariffs and financial viability. The Respondent further submits that the Petitioner’s submission that all existing beneficiaries have consented to the life extension of the project is factually inaccurate and misleading. The petition filed without the consent of APDCL is in contravention of the regulatory framework. 39. The Respondent further submits that the matter regarding the continuation or termination of the PPA with the Petitioner post Renovation & Modernization is presently under consideration by the Government of Assam, and a decision in this regard is awaited. 44. Regarding consent of the beneficiaries, the petitioner has submitted that the issue has already been discussed in the 49 th Commercial Sub-Committee Meeting of the North Eastern 47. The Petitioner is directed to keep separate details for assets which were procured during the 2019-24 tariff period and are also included in the R&M scheme.
title: Petition under Sections 61, 62, 64 as read with Section 79(1)(a) of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the proviso to Regulation 3(73) as read with Regulation 27 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms And Conditions Of Tariff) Regulations, 2019, and Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 for approval of proposal for life extension beyond the useful life in respect of the 291 MW Assam Gas Based Power Station of North Eastern Electric Power Corporation.
